title: [dist-txns] [failure-testing] unique secondary idx workload: CPU pegged on restart of a killed node
body:
Upon restart of a killed node, during distributed unique secondary index workload, the restarted node's CPU becomes pegged 100% and write workload does not recover.

1) This is a on a multi-AZ cluster running in AWS

http://172.151.44.11:7000/tablet-servers

2) It is running a Unique Secondary Index workload with version 1.1.0.2.

```
java -jar yb-sample-apps.jar --workload CassandraUniqueSecondaryIndex --nodes $CIP_ADDR -num_threads_read 1 -num_threads_write 16 --num_unique_keys 100000000 --num_writes 100000000 --nouuid
```

3) I stopped yb-tserver on 172.151.44.11. Workload dipped for a quick moment, but then recovered and kept running... no issues

4) I then restarted yb-tserver on 172.151.44.11. Tablets bootstrapped, leaders balanced, etc. But WRITES are stuck:
```
018-09-28 01:05:23,908 [INFO|com.yugabyte.sample.common.metrics.MetricsTracker|MetricsTracker] Read: 560.57 ops/sec (1.78 ms/op), 629134 total ops  |  Write: 0.00 ops/sec (0.00 ms/op), 3292175 total ops
```

Writes did not recover at all.

CPU utilization on this node was at nearly 98% and stayed that way.

Running  "perf top" highlights these top contenders on this node

```

  1.86%  librocksdb.so                   [.] rocksdb::MergingIterator::Valid

```
